images.title: Factors of 18 and of 30
images.purpose: Show the two lists of factors with the numbers in both lists joined, so the common factors of 18 and 30 are 1, 2, 3 and 6.
images.composition: Two rows of chips, the factors of 18 above and of 30 below, with four purple chips joined by lines across the rows, and the common factors written under them.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 60, the heading Common factors of 18 and 30 (48 px, bold, dark #1F2937). Two rows of number chips, each chip a rounded rectangle (corner radius 14 px) 100 by 80 px with a bold number (48 px). ROW 1, y 190 to 270, headed on the left by the text Factors of 18 (left aligned at x 100, centred at y 230, 40 px bold dark): exactly 6 chips with the numbers 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18 from left to right, the first chip starting at x 420 with 120 px from chip to chip (centres x 470, 590, 710, 830, 950, 1070). ROW 2, y 430 to 510, headed on the left by the text Factors of 30 (left aligned at x 100, centred at y 470): exactly 8 chips with the numbers 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30 from left to right, the first chip starting at x 420 with 120 px from chip to chip (centres x 470, 590, 710, 830, 950, 1070, 1190, 1310). The chips with the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 6 (in both rows, 8 chips in all) are filled reddish purple #CC79A7 with a dark #2B2B2B outline; the other 6 chips (9 and 18 in row 1; 5, 10, 15 and 30 in row 2) are white with a grey #6B7280 outline. Exactly 4 reddish purple connecting lines, 5 px thick, from the bottom of a row 1 chip (y 270) to the top of the row 2 chip with the same number (y 430): 1 from x 470 to x 470, 2 from x 590 to x 590, 3 from x 710 to x 710, and 6 from x 830 (row 1) to x 950 (row 2), a slanted line. At the bottom, centred at x 728 and y 640, the text common factors: 1, 2, 3, 6 (56 px, bold, dark #1F2937), and at y 730 the text A jump of 1, 2, 3 or 6 lands on both 18 and 30 (36 px, dark). No other text. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: The common factors of two numbers are the numbers in both lists of factors.
images.description: The factors of 18 and the factors of 30 as number chips, with 1, 2, 3 and 6 joined as the common factors.
images.context: Concept image for Common Factors of Two Numbers. It follows the idea of the common factors of 24 and 36 in your maths book (the jump sizes that reach both numbers) and uses this concept's own example, 18 and 30.
images.teaching_notes: List the factors of each number first, then join the matching chips. The slip to watch is joining only the biggest common factor and forgetting 1.

image_decisions.why: Two lists with the shared chips joined show how the common factors are picked.
